Smt. Geeta Yadav - Govt. Advocate for respondent-State.

Order 
This is second application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of the Bhartiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (Section 439 of Cr.P.C.) for grant of regular bail relating to FIR/Crime No.245/2024 dated 09.07.2024 registered at Police Station Budni District Sehore for the offence punishable under Section 376(2)(n) of IPC and Sections 66-C, 66-D and 67 of IT Act.

Earlier bail application of the applicant was dismissed as withdrawn by this Court vide order dated 24.09.2024 passed in M.Cr.C. No.37702/2024.
2.
Learned counsel for the applicant contends that the applicant and the prosecutrix were in relationship.

A perusal of statement of the prosecutrix recorded before the trial Court clearly reflect the factum of relationship with the present applicant and they stayed under the same roof for a prolong period of time.
It is contended by the counsel that none of the photographs is obscene.

It is thus, contended by the counsel that the present applicant who himself is aged about 20 years and the age of the prosecutrix was NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:12526 2 MCRC-50766-2024 undisputedly major on the date of alleged incident, the applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail 3.
Per contra, learned counsel for the State has opposed the prayer and submitted that looking to the nature of allegation, the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail.

sentences.text: 4. Heard the submissions and perused the case diary.
5. A perusal of case diary prima facie reflects that the applicant and the prosecutrix were in relationship.
The prosecutrix is major.
The applicant is in custody since 18.07.2024 and the charge-sheet in the matter has already been filed.
6. Thus, taking into consideration the totality of the circumstances of the case, this Court is of the considered view that it is a fit case to release the applicant on bail.
Therefore, without expressing any view on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.

7. It is directed that the applicant shall be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for his appearance before the said Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this regard during the pendency of trial.

8. It is further directed that the applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 480 (3) of the BNSS.
9.
Accordingly, M.Cr.C. stands disposed of.
